questions.stem: In an intercostobrachial nerve block, which spinal root does the nerve usually arise from?
The intercostobrachial nerve is usually the lateral cutaneous branch of the ____ intercostal nerve.
Why is the intercostobrachial nerve at risk during axillary surgery?
questions.answer: It runs superficially through breast tissue, lateral chest wall and axilla

questions.stem: Which other nerve shares supply of the upper half of the medial and posterior arm with the intercostobrachial nerve?
questions.answer: Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm

questions.stem: The intercostobrachial block is an adjunct to which block for medial or posterior upper arm surgery?
What does an intercostobrachial block help with when an upper arm tourniquet is used?
In the landmark intercostobrachial block, what volume of local anaesthetic is infiltrated subcutaneously?
Which needle is used for the landmark intercostobrachial block?
How is the ultrasound probe oriented for an intercostobrachial nerve block?
questions.answer: Short axis on the medial, inferior surface of the arm
